About the Project

The Quantum Informatics CDT combines doctoral research with training across computing, physics, mathematics and engineering. Its four-year programme accepts a limited number of fully funded international researchers.

Research Areas

  • Quantum computing
  • computer science
  • physics
  • mathematics and engineering

Funding and duration

ComponentDetails
FundingFull tuition including the international fee gap; Research Training Support Grant.
MaintenanceGBP 21,805/year (2026/27 reference); Home enhancement GBP 30,000/year for 2027/28
Duration4 years; September 2027 start

Eligibility and Requirements

Relevant first/2:1-equivalent degree; limited fully funded International places. English evidence required where applicable. English evidence, approved equivalents and waivers depend on the programme; IELTS is not a universal requirement for every applicant.

Application dates

ComponentDetails
RecruitmentOpen from 6 October 2026
Deadline7 January 2027

How to Apply

Apply via Edinburgh with a two-page CV, two-page statement of intent, transcripts and two references; complete the mandatory demographics survey.

A research proposal is not required at this stage: upload the statement of intent in its place. International applicants do not receive the Home-only TechFirst enhancement.

About The University of Edinburgh

The University of Edinburgh offers doctoral research across science, engineering, humanities, social sciences and health. Its research schools host scholarship competitions and doctoral training programmes with different admission and funding routes.
